name: project_summary
description: Read-only. The open GeoStrix project at a glance: its name, coordinate system, counts (holes, assay intervals, logged intervals per layer, sections), the assay elements with their units, and the data credit. Start here.

name: list_holes
description: Read-only. The drillholes of the open project, one row each: hole id, collar easting / northing / elevation (project coordinates), azimuth, dip (negative = pointing down), length, and the collar's own fields. Optionally keep only holes whose collar field equals a value. Paged: at most 200 rows per call.

field.description: A collar field to filter on (for example a drill type or a year). Leave out for every hole.

value.description: The value the field must equal (compared as text, ignoring case). Needs 'field'.

offset.description: Rows to skip, to read the next page.

name: get_hole
description: Read-only. One drillhole: its collar, the survey stations (at most 200), the logged intervals of each layer (at most 100 per layer) and how many assay intervals it has. For the assays themselves use get_assays.

hole_id.description: The hole id, exactly as list_holes gives it.

name: get_assays
description: Read-only. Assay intervals (from, to, and the grade of each element asked for) of one hole, or of every hole, optionally between two depths. Grades are in the unit the project stores them in (said in each reply). QA/QC samples (standards, blanks, duplicates) are left out. Paged: at most 200 rows per call.

hole_id.description: One hole. Leave out for every hole.

elements.description: Element symbols as project_summary lists them (for example Au, Cu). Leave out for the first few.

from.description: Only intervals ending below this depth (m).

to.description: Only intervals starting above this depth (m).

offset.description: Rows to skip, to read the next page.

name: list_layers
description: Read-only. The logs of the project (lithology, alteration, veins, structure, geotechnical ...): for each, how many intervals it holds and its most common codes with their meaning where the project has one.

name: get_layer_rows
description: Read-only. The logged intervals of one layer for one hole (from, to, code or value). Paged: at most 200 rows per call.

layer.description: The layer key list_layers gives (for example litho).

offset.description: Rows to skip, to read the next page.

name: grade_stats
description: Read-only. Statistics of one element's assay grades: count, mean, minimum, maximum, the percentiles a top cut is chosen from (90, 95, 97.5, 99, 99.5), optionally split by the code of a logged layer (for example lithology) at each sample's mid-depth. QA/QC samples are left out.

domain_layer.description: A layer key to split the statistics by (for example litho). Leave out for one set of statistics.

name: best_intercepts
description: Read-only. The best intercepts of one element at a cut-off, as the Best intercepts dialog computes them: composited from the assays with the internal dilution and the minimum length given, uncut. One row per intercept (hole, from, to, length, average grade), best first. Paged: at most 200 rows per call.

cutoff.description: The cut-off grade, in the unit the project stores the element in.

max_internal_dilution.description: Longest run of below-cut-off material allowed inside an intercept (m). Default 2.

offset.description: Rows to skip, to read the next page.

name: list_sections
description: Read-only. The cross-sections saved in the project: name, the two end points of the line, its azimuth, its length and the width of the corridor it shows.

name: get_section
description: Read-only. What lies along one saved section as text: the holes whose collars are inside its corridor, each with its distance along the line and its offset from it, and optionally the intercepts of one element at a cut-off in those holes.

section.description: The section's name (or id) as list_sections gives it.

element.description: An element symbol, to add the intercepts at 'cutoff' in the section's holes.

name: job_status
description: Read-only. Checks on a change GeoStrix started and answered 'started' (a long download, later a model run): running, done (with what it made) or failed (with why). Give the job_id from that answer; without one it lists this app's last few jobs. GeoStrix shows each change in its own window when it is done.

name: suggest_trend
description: Read-only. The trend helper's suggestion for this project: up to four candidate trends (a plane the geology or the grade runs along), each with its strength (strong, fair or weak), its reasons and its warnings, the best one marked suggested. Read from the measured structures, the logged unit tops, the grades of one element and the drilling itself (a plane that is only the drill pattern is said so, weak, and never suggested). Modelled surfaces, outcrop readings and mapped contacts are not read here: the Modelling tab's trend helper also reads them. These are suggestions from the data, not facts. It only reads: setting a trend is done in GeoStrix.

element.description: An assay element's symbol: its grades at or above their 90th percentile are one source. Without it the grades are not read.

name: list_drill_programs
description: Read-only. The project's drill programs (GeoStrix's Drill program, in Targeting > Planned holes): for each, when it was made, its element and rule, its versions, how many holes it suggested, whether they were added as planned holes, how many are drilled, and whether new data came in since. Exploration targeting, not a resource estimate.

name: get_drill_program
description: Read-only. One drill program: its holes in suggested drilling order (pad, collar, azimuth, dip, length, cost, score, whether above the diminishing-returns line, and why it is there in a sentence GeoStrix computed), each hole's prediction (chance of an intercept, grade x metres low / middle / high = P10 / P50 / P90, a typical hit), the drilled results against their range and the calibration, and the cautions to pass on. Per-hole grade x metres only: no tonnes, not a resource.

version.description: A version number; without it the latest.

name: explain_hole
description: Read-only. Why a planned hole is where it is: its design, the reason the drill program gave, the nearest drilled collar, its prediction and whether it is still current (or the hole has moved, or is drilled), and the drilled result against the prediction. Build any explanation from these facts, not from guesses.

hole.description: A planned hole's id or name.

name: predict_hole
description: Read-only. What a hole would probably cut, from the drilled composites: the chance of an intercept at the cut-off and grade x metres low / middle / high (P10 / P50 / P90 of 200 runs of a kriging-based grade model, the settings of the newest Grade estimation run or its defaults). Give a planned hole, or a collar with azimuth, dip and length. It computes for a few seconds and keeps nothing. The range comes from the hole spacing and the variogram only; it is exploration targeting, not a resource estimate.

hole.description: A planned hole's id or name (or give collar, azimuth, dip and length).

dip.description: Negative for a hole pointing down.

element.description: The element; without it the newest Grade estimation run's, else the first assayed.

cutoff.description: The intercept cut-off in the element's unit; without it the composites' upper quartile.

internal_dilution.description: The longest gap bridged inside an intercept, metres.

name: make_section
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: adds a new cross-section to the project (it shows in StrixViewer's section list), either between two points in the project's coordinates (list_holes gives the collars') or through one hole in its own plane. Nothing is replaced: a name already used gets ' (2)'. Undo in GeoStrix takes it back.

name.description: The section's name. Leave out for GeoStrix's own ('Section 1000E 2000N az 90°' / 'Section through DH-23-001 (az 90°)').

along_hole.description: A hole id: the section runs through this hole along its bearing (instead of 'from' and 'to').

corridor_m.description: The buffer: holes within this distance of the line are drawn (m). Default 100.

name: make_sheet
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: adds a new Layout page, one of Layout's one-click sheets: 'plan' (every checked hole on a drill plan with a legend, north arrow and scale bar), 'section' (the newest section picture sent to Layout), 'log' (the newest strip log sent to Layout) or 'intercepts' (the newest Best intercepts table in Layout). The page is printed or exported by the user, from GeoStrix. The toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

name: add_best_intercepts
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: computes the best intercepts of one element at a cut-off, exactly as the read tool best_intercepts does (the lab assays without the QC samples, uncut, best first by grade x length), and puts them as a table, with its caveats, on a new Layout page named 'Best intercepts'. The toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes the page.

cutoff.description: The cut-off grade, in the unit the project stores the element in.

max_internal_dilution.description: Longest run of below-cut-off material allowed inside an intercept (m). Default 2.

name: fetch_satellite_image
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: downloads the latest clear Copernicus Sentinel-2 natural-colour image over the project area and adds it as a new raster (Maps). The area is the loaded terrain's when there is one (so the image matches it), else around the drillholes. GeoStrix first asks the user, every time, whether to download; a refusal is answered 'The user declined the download in GeoStrix.'. It can take a minute or more: after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). The toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

max_cloud_percent.description: The most cloud a scene's catalogue entry may report (%). Default 30.

area.description: 'terrain' (the default, when a terrain is loaded) or 'holes' (around the drillholes).

name: fetch_terrain
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: downloads Copernicus GLO-30 terrain over the project area (around the drillholes, as Maps › Terrain opens on) and adds it as the project's terrain, with GeoStrix's check of the collars against the ground (a large misfit is reported, the project's coordinate system is never changed). Refused when a terrain is already loaded (nothing is overwritten). GeoStrix first asks the user, every time, whether to download. It can take a minute or more: after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). The toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

name: colour_holes
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: changes how StrixViewer draws the holes. by 'field': the holes (collars and traces) coloured by a collar field, with a legend; 'element': that element's grades shown along the holes (StrixViewer's assay display, that element alone); 'layer': a logged layer (a key list_layers gives) shown along the holes, coloured by its codes; 'none': the holes in one colour. Only the view changes, nothing in the project's data. The toast's Undo in GeoStrix puts it back.

name.description: The element symbol, the layer key or the collar field (as list_holes shows the fields). Not needed with 'none'.

name: show_layers
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: shows or hides layers in StrixViewer: logged layers by the keys list_layers gives, 'assays' (the assay display) and 'terrain'. Only the view changes. A key that is not found is listed in the answer. The toast's Undo in GeoStrix puts it back.

visible.description: true to show them, false to hide them.

name: set_view
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: points StrixViewer's 3D view: 'fit' (the Fit button: the data shown), 'top' (plan, looking down), 'bottom' (looking up), 'hole' (zoomed to one hole: 'target' is its id) or 'section' (opens a saved section in its own window, as its row in the list does: 'target' is its name). The toast's Undo in GeoStrix puts the camera back.

target.description: A hole id (view 'hole') or a section name (view 'section').

name: build_surface
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: builds one logged rock as a 3D surface, as StrixViewer's Model > Start here does with Build it for me, by the rock's role in Modelling codes: Intrusions and bodies (a solid shape from where the holes cut it) for an intrusion, dyke, vein or breccia; Cover and weathering (its base) for overburden; otherwise Rock layers, which builds the surfaces between all the rocks that lie in a steady order down the holes (the rock named must be one of them). The model's size and detail are read from the logs. A rock the data cannot support is refused, saying what to mark first. One model at a time; it can take minutes (the status bar shows its progress and Cancel): after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). It adds a surface and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

rock.description: The rock's code as logged (list_layers and get_layer_rows show them).

name: add_block_model
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: adds the last model's lithology blocks as a block model, as the Result block's Add as block model does (cells above every modelled top are left out; the model is not the logs). Needs the last model's blocks to exist (built in GeoStrix from the surfaces, or a GemPy model): without them it says so. For a grade shell's cells use add_grade_shell_blocks; for grades estimated into blocks, build_grade_estimate. A very large model is confirmed with the user in GeoStrix first. It adds a block model and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

name: build_grade_shell
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: builds a grade shell for one element, as StrixViewer's Model > Start here > Grade model does with Build it for me: a shell around the grades above a cut-off read from the assays, with cells and a search sized from the drilling. It is a picture of where the grade is, not a resource estimate. One model at a time; it can take minutes (the status bar shows its progress and Cancel): after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). It adds a shell and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

element.description: The assay element's symbol (project_summary lists them).

name: build_grade_estimate
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: estimates one element's grades into a block model with StrixViewer's Grade estimation dialog, opened in GeoStrix: the element chosen, the dialog's own settings from the data (cell, search, the block budget, how unsampled metres are read; what it kept from the last estimate in this project), Run, then Add to project. A run the dialog would not start (over the block budget, a choice it still needs, a weak variogram question) is refused with its reason, and the dialog stays open for the user. The answer gives the block model, its method, cell and search, the result's lines as the dialog shows them (data support, extrapolation, single-hole blocks...) and its 'Not a resource estimate.' paragraph word for word: it is not a Mineral Resource. One model at a time; it can take minutes (the status bar shows its progress and Cancel): after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). It adds a block model and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

element.description: The assay element's symbol (project_summary lists them).

name: add_grade_shell_blocks
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: adds the last grade shell built in this session (build_grade_shell, or Grade shell in GeoStrix) as a block model: its own grid cells at or above its cut-off, after its ground cut, each with the shell's interpolated grade (a shell with an envelope area gives 1 inside: an envelope is a probability, not grades). A shell opened with a saved project, removed, or built along a structural trend is refused, naming build_grade_estimate for grades in blocks. A picture of where the grade is, not a resource estimate. It adds a block model and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

name: build_vein
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: builds one vein or dyke as a thin sheet through the places where the holes cut it, as StrixViewer's Model > Start here > Veins and dykes does with Build it for me. The code is one of the Veins log, or a lithology code read as a vein or dyke (Modelling codes). Refused with the card's verdict when the data cannot support a sheet: fewer than three holes cut it, or it is logged many times down each hole (a vein set: split it in Modelling codes, or show it with build_alteration's halo). One model at a time; it can take minutes (the status bar shows its progress and Cancel): after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). It adds a surface and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

code.description: The vein or dyke code as logged (list_layers and get_layer_rows show them).

name: build_alteration
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: builds an alteration halo for one code of the Alteration log, as StrixViewer's Alteration pane does: the volume round the intervals with that code, closed between the holes by the other alteration logged, sized from the hole spacing. Refused with a plain verdict when fewer than three holes log the code, or when no other alteration is logged to close it. One model at a time; it can take minutes (the status bar shows its progress and Cancel): after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). It adds a surface and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes it.

code.description: The alteration code as logged (list_layers and get_layer_rows show them).

name: guide_status
description: Read-only. Where the open project is in StrixViewer's guided modelling (Model > Start here): each of its seven steps (your data, area and detail, rocks and order, compute or draw, faults and veins, volumes and grade, check it) as done, next, waiting or not needed with its reason and what it offers; the step to do next; the route it suggests for building the surfaces (compute from the logs, draw, or from the geological map) and why; and the one question the guide would ask there, with its suggested answer. Read from the project's tables with the guide card's own readers, so it matches the card; nothing is built. Works without 'Allow AI apps to make changes'. Use it before a build tool to choose one.

name: build_fault
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: builds one fault as flat sheeted planes through the fault evidence the holes hold, with the Faults pane's own build (StrixViewer, 3D Modelling > Faults): oriented fault picks and logged fault intervals on the holes, and outcrop fault measurements, placed as the pane places them; the planes are grouped into parallel sheets, each clipped to the ground and to the model box (or, with extent 'finite', to the evidence plus a margin). A mapped, drawn or section fault line is named in 'evidence' and must be the only one of its kind (each line is its own fault in the pane: build several there). Refused with the pane's own verdict when there is too little: no evidence, points on one line (give a dip and dip_direction), nothing inside the extent. The answer gives each sheet's dip and how far its points miss it, what was left out, and says in a warning when the fault is a guess (few points or one hole), reads as folded, or has a sheet that does not fit its points well (a typical miss over 10 m, the pane's own Check distance): do not call such a fault good. Through the box a fault runs past its evidence: there it is extrapolated, not observed. It needs no solver, so it answers at once. It adds surfaces and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes exactly them.

name.description: The fault's name (surfaces are named 'Fault: <name>'). Leave out for 'Fault 1'.

evidence.description: The kinds of evidence to use: pick (oriented fault picks in core), logged (logged fault intervals), outcrop (outcrop fault measurements), mapped, drawn, string (one line each). Leave out for pick, logged and outcrop.

extent.description: 'box': through the model box (the pane's default). 'finite': an ellipse around the evidence plus margin_m.

margin_m.description: With extent 'finite': the margin round the evidence, in metres (default 200).

sheet_gap_m.description: Sheets closer than this along their normal are one sheet (default 25 m).

dip.description: A dip for evidence with no orientation (points on one line). Needs dip_direction.

dip_direction.description: The dip's direction, degrees clockwise from north. Needs dip.

name: model_from_map
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: builds a 3D stratigraphic model from the geological map and the outcrop measurements alone, by running StrixViewer's Model from map pane as a person would (3D Modelling > Model from map): the map's own age order when most units carry an age (else bedding younging), the contact relation you choose (Conformable, the default, or Erosional), and the faults the pane's own 'Pick for me' keeps when the map has more than GemPy takes; then Build the model (GemPy). It is refused with the pane's own reason when there is no geological map with units, no terrain, fewer than two units in the order, no orientation to build from, or more units than GemPy takes (the pane offers a cut: take it in GeoStrix). The answer gives the order used and why, the relation, the faults, and the fit card's numbers: how much of the mapped ground the model matches, unit by unit, and the units that were not scored. A low fit is a finding, not an error: say so. One model at a time; it takes minutes (the status bar shows its progress and Cancel): after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status; GeoStrix shows when it is done). It adds the model's surfaces and two map pictures and replaces nothing; the toast's Undo in GeoStrix removes exactly them.

map.description: The geological map (polygons) by name. Leave out for the pane's own choice: a mapped layer that is shown.

order_from.description: 'age': the map's own ages (the default when most units carry one). 'bedding': bedding younging.

relation.description: Conformable: one shared field, units cannot pinch out (the default). Erosional: each unit truncates those below; same-age neighbours go in one package.

faults.description: 'auto' (the default): the line layer with the most fault lines. 'none': no faults. Or a line layer's name. More faults than GemPy takes: the pane's Pick for me keeps the ones that matter and says why.

name: run_drill_planner
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: suggests a drill program from the drilled pads, as the Drill program section does, and saves it in the project as a suggestion. It adds no hole: add_program_holes does, after you ask the user. Each candidate hole is scored by the rule per dollar (per metre with no drilling rate): balanced (the default: middle grade x metres plus kappa x its spread), hit (the chance of an intercept), metal (expected grade x metres) or learn (where the model knows least, for step-outs); holes are chosen one by one as if the ones before were drilled. Anywhere the model reaches: a target solid is chosen in GeoStrix itself. It can take a minute: after about 20 seconds the answer is 'started' with a job_id (check it with job_status). The answer has each hole's reason and prediction and the cautions to pass on: exploration targeting, not a resource estimate; a suggestion, not an optimum. One Undo in GeoStrix takes it back.

element.description: The element; without it the newest Grade estimation run's, else the first assayed.

rule.description: How a hole's value is scored, per dollar.

kappa.description: For balanced: 0 near known grade, 2 into the unknown (default 0.5).

cutoff.description: The intercept cut-off in the element's unit; without it the composites' upper quartile.

internal_dilution.description: The longest gap bridged inside an intercept, metres.

max_metres.description: A limit on the program's metres.

budget.description: In the project currency; needs a drilling rate in GeoStrix.

azimuth_step.description: Degrees between the directions tried from each pad (default 45).

hole_type.description: The hole type whose drilling rate prices the holes.

accept_weak_fit.description: Only after the user agreed: run even when the grade model's variogram fits weakly.

name: add_program_holes
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: adds a suggested program's holes as proposed planned holes, named by the project's own hole series, each with its prediction kept on it. Ask the user before calling it. It adds and replaces nothing; one Undo in GeoStrix takes them all back.

holes.description: 'all' (the default), 'above_line' (above the diminishing-returns line), or the holes' order numbers separated by commas, e.g. '1,2,5'.

name: set_planned_hole_status
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: marks a planned hole proposed or approved. Never drilled: a hole becomes drilled only when the geologist links its as-drilled hole in GeoStrix. One Undo in GeoStrix takes it back.

hole.description: A planned hole's id or name.

name: list_rasters_surveys
description: Read-only. The grids and images, point surveys and surface samples the open project holds, and the anomaly thresholds already saved: each raster's id, name, kind (grid or picture), survey method, unit, cells and who made it (a filter, a gridding); each point survey's name, method and points; the surface samples' count, media and elements. Lists are cut at 100. Use it to name things for the other tools.

name: suggest_thresholds
description: Read-only. The Thresholds pane's candidate rules for one element: for each population (a sampling medium, or all the assays) the value of each rule (percentiles, median + 2 MAD, Tukey fence, probability-plot break... on log axes; mean + 2 SD and the break on the values for a major element), the rules a population cannot reach, the rule the pane would open on, and the threshold already saved. These are candidate rules from the data, not facts: the geologist decides what is anomalous. It only reads: saving one is set_threshold.

element.description: The element's symbol, as a surface-sample or an assay element.

source.description: Which data: the surface samples (soil, stream, rock chip) or the drill assays. Without it the surface samples, else the drill assays.

name: set_threshold
description: Makes a change in GeoStrix: saves one of suggest_thresholds' rules as an element's anomaly threshold, the record the Thresholds pane saves (one value per population, the rule, its date), which the anomaly maps print in their legends. Nothing is replaced: if a threshold is already saved for the element (and source) the call is refused, and the user changes it in Thresholds. A rule a population cannot reach is refused with the reason. One Undo in GeoStrix takes it back.

rule.description: A rule id suggest_thresholds gave (for example median2mad or p95).

source.description: Which data: the surface samples or the drill assays. Without it the surface samples, else the drill assays.
